scenarios.name: Required deletion preserves commissioned framework coverage
scenarios.draft:
Our school should add a quiet lunch table because some students want a calmer place to eat. For example, my friend could read there after eating. In the class survey, 24 of 40 students said they would use it. This shows that many students are interested.

A quiet table could make lunch more comfortable for those students.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Using the assigned passage, argue whether our school should add a quiet lunch table. Include one reason supported by the passage and explain the survey result.
scenarios.teacher_directions: Include the class survey result and explain how it supports your claim.
scenarios.source_material: A synthetic class survey asked 40 students whether they would use a quiet lunch table. 24 said yes. The survey did not ask about grades or behavior.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Required narrowing retains exact requirement evidence, live task alignment, and every commissioned framework component
expected_outcomes: Classify required narrowing with exact deleted text and commissioned requirement evidence.
Retain a live task-alignment issue and framework coverage for both commissioned components.
Do not call required deletion fully addressed or replace the live candidate with coverage alone.

strengths: The draft states a specific proposal.

scenarios.name: Strong draft permits optional-only direct response
scenarios.draft:
Our school should add a quiet reading period because it gives students time to practice choosing and enjoying books. During a recent synthetic class discussion, several students said interruptions made sustained reading difficult. A short scheduled period would protect that focus while still allowing teachers to offer help. This routine would support reading without replacing regular instruction.

The period could also give students a calm place to reflect on what they read and share reccomendations with classmates.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Argue whether our school should add a quiet reading period.
scenarios.teacher_directions: State a claim, give a relevant reason, and explain it.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Direct response with no manufactured issue and only genuinely optional exact-located polish
expected_outcomes: Do not manufacture a meaningful issue or continue revision merely to provide candidates.
Use direct response with empty issues; any optional polish must be low stakes and exactly located.
Do not claim mastery or submission readiness.

optional_polish: Routine spelling support for the intentional typo; optional concision or enrichment only if the reviewer agrees it is not meaningful

scenarios.name: Ordinary task difficulty remains writing support
scenarios.draft:
Our school should start a community garden because it would give students fresh food. In the synthetic class survey, 62% of students said they would try vegetables from a school garden. This result shows that some students are interested in fresh food.

A garden would also give students shared jobs such as watering plants and pulling weeds.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Argue whether our school should start a community garden using the supplied survey.
scenarios.teacher_directions: Include a clear claim and explain your evidence.
scenarios.source_material: An anonymous synthetic class survey asked 50 students whether they would try vegetables from a school garden. 31 students (62%) said yes. The survey measured interest, not health outcomes.
scenarios.student_concerns: This is hard. I want to explain my evidence more clearly.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Ordinary task difficulty does not trigger serious-discouragement review
expected_outcomes: Provide bounded writing support for a draft-supported concern.
Do not infer serious discouragement from 'This is hard.'
Preserve source limits and student authorship.

unsupported_concerns: Serious discouragement inferred from ordinary task difficulty

expected_outcomes: Use teacher_review with serious_discouragement and factual evidence.
